spot: Left Face climbing area (Sections 1-2) - end of the cables

detail.reason: This is the cliff BASE (standable bottom of the wall), not a high overlook; you stand below the rock, no long view down.
At the base of a quarry wall the view is enclosed by the cliff, not a broad sweeping vista.
Corners, roofs and a 'leaky roof' overhang create sheltered above-ground rock recesses to reach into - exact niche profile.
Niches and ledges at the cliff base let the box rest against natural stone at/above ground, no digging.
The operative feature is the granite-gneiss crag/corner itself - stone is the host feature throughout.
No creek/pond adjacent to the west cliff base; nearest water (wetland, Grindstone crossing) is elsewhere.
Trail approaches around the wooded left side, but the spot itself is at a bare cut rock wall, not a forest/clearing edge.
Reached on an established trail around the left side to the end of the cables, then turn right - off-trail-adjacent, easy footing.
Standing at the base needs no climbing; well under 3 mi from Rocky Face Church Rd, no water crossing.
Left/west corner around the side of the crag is off the main view, but it is a known, named, frequented climbing area.
A cliff corner/roof is not a saddle or notch between paired crags framing a view.
No prominent tree marker noted; the marker is rock/cliff, not an oak or pine.
Explicitly WEST-side exposure - opposite of the east-facing cue.
Quarry-cut walls, corners and roofs are angular/blocky, not rounded or domed.
Quarry seeps/cliffs host saxifrage and lichen elsewhere; nothing specific noted for this corner, weak.
Host is granitic gneiss (quartz/feldspar bearing) so crystalline in a broad sense, but not a quartz/sparkle marker.
Quarry-cut vertical walls, corners, roofs and blocky rampart form are sharply angular/faceted - strong match.
Grey granitic gneiss; no reddish/iron or golden warm-stone cue for this spot.
Granite-gneiss is light grey, mildly pale, but not a distinctive white/quartz-white marker.
A 'leaky roof' overhang is an undercut, not a bowl/cup/basin depression.
No watercourse junction or bend at this dry west cliff base.
Approach is a level walk around the side, not a descent into a draw nor ending high.
Bolts/anchors and route placards exist as man-made marks, but these are modern climbing hardware, not a subtle confirming seam.
Approach is explicitly the LEFT side of the mountain ('Left Face') - directly matches the left-turn nudge.
Cliff-base corners/roofs are sheltered enough to protect a box yet open to weather (buzzards roost here), not a sealed cave.
'End of the cables, then turn right' is a fixed locatable point a count could run from, but no numeric value given.
